overall_assessment: Steiner's text-splitting extraction is largely correct for the sections it does capture (learning_outcomes, course_content, coursework_requirements, assessment), but suffers from three consistent structural defects: (1) the heading word 'Vurdering' is invariably appended as a trailing artefact to every coursework_requirements row, (2) assessment rows absorb exam-logistics boilerplate (sensorordning, hjelpemidler, ny/utsatt eksamen) that the codebook excludes, and (3) PDF-origin page numbers bleed into extracted text throughout. The teaching_methods section is never extracted even when an 'Arbeidsmåter' heading is present; in one case that content leaks into course_content instead. Learning outcomes are silently truncated when they are long.

Vurdering
findings.description: Every coursework_requirements row ends with the bare heading word 'Vurdering'. The text-splitter uses 'Vurdering' as the boundary token to end the coursework_requirements segment, but it includes the token itself in the output rather than stopping before it. This is not content; it is a dangling section heading from the following section.
findings.root_cause_hypothesis: The heading-boundary split in the text-splitting strategy is inclusive (regex keeps the matched heading). The split point for 'Vurdering' should be exclusive (cut before the heading, not after).
findings.suggested_fix: Change the coursework_requirements split to stop before the 'Vurdering' heading: use a negative lookahead or trim the trailing 'Vurdering' token from the coursework_requirements segment after splitting.

findings.description: The assessment section consistently absorbs exam-logistics boilerplate that the codebook explicitly excludes: 'Sensurordning'/'Sensorordning' (grading committee), 'Tillatte hjelpemidler'/'Hjelpemidler til eksamen' (permitted aids), 'Vurderingsuttrykk' (grade scale), and 'Ny/utsatt eksamen' (re-sit rules). The codebook states 'exclude exam-logistics tables (specific dates, rooms, registration deadlines) — keep only the assessment design.' Grade-scale text and sensor/re-sit boilerplate fall squarely in the logistics category.
findings.root_cause_hypothesis: The text-splitter captures everything between the 'Vurdering/Eksamensform' heading and the end of the document (or next major heading), making no attempt to exclude the standard administrative sub-headings that follow the exam-form description.
findings.suggested_fix: After extracting assessment text, strip content from these sub-headings through end of their paragraph: 'Sensurordning', 'Sensorordning', 'Tillatte hjelpemidler', 'Hjelpemidler til eksamen', 'Vurderingsuttrykk', 'Ny/utsatt eksamen'. Alternatively, capture only the text up to the first of these sub-headings.

findings.description: Several learning_outcomes rows are silently truncated mid-sentence (marked '[truncated N chars]' in the packet). The full outcome lists in the ground-truth plans are complete; the extractor stops before capturing all items under Ferdigheter and/or Generell kompetanse. Affected courses tend to have longer outcome sections (2000+ chars). The codebook requires every individual outcome statement to be captured.
findings.root_cause_hypothesis: The text-splitting strategy likely applies a character or token cap per section row. When learning_outcomes exceeds this cap the remainder is silently dropped rather than split into continuation rows.
findings.suggested_fix: Remove or raise the per-section character cap for learning_outcomes. If a cap is needed for downstream processing, split into multiple rows (one per Kunnskap/Ferdigheter/Generell kompetanse group) rather than truncating.

findings.description: Bare page numbers ('9', '10', '11', '12', etc.) from the PDF source appear as standalone lines inside extracted sections — most visibly in learning_outcomes and course_content. These are PDF artefacts with no content value and pollute downstream text use.
findings.root_cause_hypothesis: The PDF-to-text conversion preserves page-break headers/footers as bare digit lines. The text-splitting strategy makes no attempt to filter them.
findings.suggested_fix: Add a pre-processing step that strips lines matching /^\d{1,3}$/ (standalone 1-3 digit numbers) that appear at the start or end of a paragraph boundary, or use a regex to remove them globally from the raw extracted text before sectioning.

findings.description: Course 9 (PEL1.5 / FoU-oppgave) has an explicit 'Arbeidsmåter' heading whose content (writing seminar, supervision, self-study, oral presentation) clearly belongs to teaching_methods per the codebook. The extractor assigned this text to course_content instead. No teaching_methods row was emitted. In other courses, teaching methods are embedded in the course description or absent, so the impact is limited to cases where an 'Arbeidsmåter' heading is present.
findings.root_cause_hypothesis: The heading map does not include 'Arbeidsmåter' as a trigger for teaching_methods; the heading is either unknown to the splitter or falls inside the Innhold block, causing it to be consumed by course_content.
findings.suggested_fix: Add 'Arbeidsmåter' to the heading-to-section map pointing to teaching_methods. If the splitter processes headings in order, ensure 'Arbeidsmåter' is checked before the Innhold/course_content boundary is closed.
